{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = "/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Confirm the premises
assert set(data['converted'].unique()) == {0, 1}, "'converted' should only have 0 and 1"
assert set(data['status'].unique()) == {'completed', 'refunded'}, "'status' should only have 'completed' and 'refunded'"
assert (data['customer_age'] == -1).sum() == 108, "108 missing ages expected"

# Filter for converted customers
converted_data = data[data['converted'] == 1]

# Check for refunded orders among converted
refunded_converted = converted_data[converted_data['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f"Number of converted orders that were refunded: {len(refunded_converted)}")

# Clean revenue column
# Remove commas and convert to float
data['revenue'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check for QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == 999999.99]
print(f"Number of QA orders (revenue = 999999.99): {len(qa_orders)}")

# But for this question, we only care about customer age of converted customers
# Exclude refunded converted orders (they are invalid for age calculation)
converted_valid = converted_data[converted_data['status'] == 'completed']

# Now, compute mean age, excluding -1 (missing)
valid_ages = converted_valid['customer_age'][converted_valid['customer_age'] != -1]
mean_age = valid_ages.mean()

print(f"Mean age of converted customers (excluding -1 and refunded): {mean_age}")"}
